title: Labseed SDK orientation manifest + sprint checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
A compact manifest for a 1-day "labseed" onboarding sprint for new integrators (internal & pilot customers). Focus: get a working sample app calling Redwood API, capture telemetry, run a tiny smoke harness, and document the first three failure modes. This is intentionally opinionated and minimal — goal is confidence, not completeness.

Audience
---
- New SDK adopters (engineers at customer or internal solutions engineers)
- Field SEs running quick pilots
- Developer advocates prepping demo apps

Success criteria (end of day)
---
1) Working sample app that can do a text generation or embed call end-to-end (local dev -> Redwood hosted API).
2) Basic telemetry: per-request latency, token count, error type and a synthetic quality metric (prompt/response hash).
3) Smoke harness ran 50 synthetic requests and passed non-flaky thresholds.
4) Short failure-cards doc listing top 3 reproducible failures and remediation.

High-level flow (3 modules)
---
Module A: Quickwire (30–45 min)
- Install minimal SDK (npm/pip) and run the "hello-world" quickrunner.
- Verify credentials: guidance for env var vs token file.
- Minimal code snippet: call text.generate with short prompt, print latency and token usage.
- Notes: include common local network pitfalls (proxy env, corp firewall).

Module B: Telemetry sampler + smoke harness (60 min)
- Drop-in telemetry shim (JS/Python): wraps calls to record start/end, token counts, status, and response fingerprint.
- Config: sample sampling rate 100% for pilot, retention local file -> upload later.
- Run smoke harness: 50 requests across 3 prompt classes (short, medium, multi-turn). Check failure rate < 3%.
- Collect flame graph of latencies (rough buckets: <50ms, 50–200ms, 200–800ms, >800ms).

Module C: Field polish + failure-cards (60 min)
- Add simple retry policy with exponential backoff for 429/5xx.
- Add fallback to smaller model variant when latency > 1s for two consecutive requests.
- Write 3 failure cards (repro steps, logs to capture, suggested mitigations).

Playbook checklist (tick items during the sprint)
---
- [ ] SDK installed and version pinned in repo (example: sdk@0.9.2-alpha)
- [ ] API key loaded and validated
- [ ] Basic generation call returns 200 and tokens counted
- [ ] Telemetry shim instrumented and logs showing start/stop
- [ ] Smoke harness executed (50 reqs) and results saved
- [ ] Retry/backoff implemented for transient errors
- [ ] Simple model-fallback rule implemented
- [ ] Failure cards created and attached to PR
- [ ] Short demo recorded (screen capture) for handoff

Quick code snippets (working notes)
---
# JS (pseudo)
const r = require('@redwood/sdk')
const client = r.init(process.env.RW_API_KEY)
const t0 = Date.now()
const res = await client.text.generate({model:'gemini-lite', prompt:'Summarize: release notes'})
console.log('latency', Date.now()-t0, 'tokens', res.meta.token_count)

Telemetry shim checklist (minimal fields)
---
- request_id (uuid)
- route/model
- start_ts, end_ts
- token_input_count, token_output_count
- status_code / error_class
- response_hash (sha1 of response body)

Failure-cards (examples for the sprint)
---
1) "Proxy hang": local dev behind corporate proxy -> requests time out after 30s\- Repro: set HTTP_PROXY to internal proxy and run 10 short requests\- Logs to capture: tcpdump for 30s, sdk debug log\- Mitigation: doc common env vars and add fallback to fetch via curl for smoke test

2) "Token misuse": API key with wrong scope -> 401 with ambiguous message\- Repro: use old token from tests account\- Logs: SDK token validation trace, server response body\- Mitigation: add richer client-side validation and link to token rotation doc

3) "Burst throttle": quick burst of 200 requests -> intermittent 429s\- Repro: run harness with r=200 qps for 10s\- Logs: 429 rate limit header values, per-route telemetry\- Mitigation: client-side leaky-bucket and doc note: request bursts, consider request shaping

Open questions / TODOs
---
- Where should the telemetry uploads land for pilots? (temp s3 prefix vs attach to Confluence page) -- @Marco to decide
- Small SDK helper for quick model-fallback exists in python only; need parity in JS (Priya)
- Decide whether to include a pre-baked docker image for in-office demos (pro: deterministic env; con: size)
- Should the smoke harness use realistic prompt corpus (redacted customer prompts) or synthetic prompts? Need legal OK for any customer-derived corpus.

Handoff & follow-up
---
- Create PR with the sample app & harness under examples/labseed-onramp
- Attach failure-cards to JIRA:RWD-3112 as sub-tasks
- Schedule 30min sync with Field SEs to iterate on the Quickwire script and telemetry fields

Notes to self (scratch)
---
- Keep the quickwire under 45 minutes; if people get stuck at proxy step, move to inside-corp wifi or provide prerecorded demo video
- Try to reduce friction of token validation: include "rw-cli auth check" small tool
- Consider a "first-5-requests" friendly UX: preflight that runs 5 tiny requests and surfaces common config mistakes

Appendix: quick links
---
- token rotation doc (confluence:RDW-Security-Auth-23)
- sample harness PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter/pulls/123
- quick demo video (internal Dropbox link)

-- end of draft --
